event.description: Use one transpose-tied square transform for both feed-forward projections
event.proposal: Family: parameter tying. Current retained frontier is 1,672 parameters at 99.010000%, a +0.010000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 39 prior macro-attempts and 449 prior micro-trials in this family. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0095/micro-0001, a block-0 pre-FF bias union retained at 1,672 parameters and 99.01%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0096/micro-0001, whose pre-attention scale union scored 98.90%. Hypothesis: the square width-16 GELU feed-forward path can use one learned feature transform and its transpose for residual reconstruction, eliminating an independently learned output map while preserving nonlinear width and depth sharing. This is a major representational tying change, not scalar pruning: the two current grouped 16x16 maps are projected to one dense 16x16 matrix by averaging the input map with the output transpose, yielding 1,465 parameters. It is more informative than the nearest untested same-orientation tie because transpose tying aligns analysis and synthesis coordinates and is the least disruptive autoencoder-like constraint for a square bottleneck. Attention, normalization, autoregressive logits, and generic decoding remain unchanged.
